title: Unified API Key Fleet Management and Expiry Automation
creator: Lina Chen
description: Deliver a unified platform-level service and admin surface for API key and token governance that enforces naming conventions, per-scope key issuance, automated expiry/rotation, and integrated audit log signals. This work ties RBAC v2 identities to token issuance and lifecycle, provides an automated sweep-and-rotate daemon for stale credentials, extends audit logging hooks for every issuance/rotation/revocation event, and exposes controls in the Console and Admin API. Goal is to reduce leaked/stale-token risk, simplify operator workflows, and make token lifecycle auditable for compliance audits.
background: Current token tooling is fragmented: service keys, machine tokens, and legacy API keys are governed by multiple ad-hoc scripts and different naming patterns. There have been multiple incidents where long-lived tokens remained active past role changes. RBAC-v2 introduces scoped principals; we need a first-class token fleet manager that issues per-scope keys, enforces TTL/expiry, automates rotation, and writes structured events to audit logs for SSO/SAML and admin actions. This ticket covers backend service, API, Console UX, and rollout plan (migration for existing keys).
acceptance_criteria: Service: token-fleet-manager deployed in staging and production with health checks and SLOs documented
API: /admin/tokens endpoints for create/rotate/revoke/list supporting per-scope keys and name metadata
Rotation: automated background sweep rotates keys older than policy TTL and emits audit events; rotation can be scheduled or immediate via API
Naming policy: tokens must conform to company convention; system rejects non-conformant names and suggests migration mapping
Migration: migration script that marks existing legacy keys, creates replacement per-scope keys, and revokes old tokens with rollback path
Audit: all create/rotate/revoke events appear in audit logs with structured fields (actor, scope, key_id, old_key_id, reason, correlation_id)
Console: Admin Console shows token fleet table, filters by scope, last rotated, owner, and provides one-click rotate/revoke actions
RBAC integration: token issuance respects RBAC-v2 permission checks and inherits effective permissions from principal at issuance time
Security review: completed with remediation items resolved and security sign-off attached to ticket
tasks: Design: finalize token-fleet-manager architecture and data model (TTL, scope, name, rotation metadata)
Backend: implement fleet manager service with gRPC and REST-facing admin endpoints
DB: migration for token metadata table and indexing for queries by owner/scope/age
Audit: add structured audit event schema and wire events into central audit pipeline
Console: build token fleet UI, filters, rotation modal, and bulk actions
API: add SDK helpers and CLI for scheduled rotation jobs
Migration: write and test migration tool for legacy tokens; include canary run and rollback plan
Monitoring: SLOs, alerting, dashboards for rotation success rate and stale-token count
Runbook: write incident runbook for token compromise and emergency revocation
